title: FAA Part 107 decision-making, crew resource management and physiology practice questions
description: Free Part 107 practice questions on decision-making, risk, crew resource management, stress, fatigue and fitness to fly, linked to FAA sources.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what can hyperventilation lead to, and why?

options.A: Hypoxia, because the pilot is flying at high altitude
options.B: Dehydration, because water is lost through rapid breathing
options.C: Unconsciousness, due to the respiratory system's overriding mechanism to regain control of breathing
options.D: A slower heart rate, because carbon dioxide builds up in the blood

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says hyperventilation "seldom incapacitates completely", but "Hyperventilation can lead to unconsciousness due to the respiratory system’s overriding mechanism to regain control of breathing."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: A remote pilot who does not know about hyperventilation is alarmed by its symptoms and starts breathing even faster. According to the Study Guide, what do the increased breathing rate and anxiety do?

options.A: They further aggravate the problem
options.B: They restore the proper carbon dioxide level in the body
options.C: They have no effect on the condition
options.D: They end the condition once the flight is over

questions.explanation: Hyperventilation "causes disturbing symptoms that can alarm the uninformed pilot. In such cases, increased breathing rate and anxiety further aggravate the problem."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Fitness to fly and the medical condition rule
questions.question: A remote pilot has a medical condition, such as epilepsy, that may create a risk to operations. According to the Study Guide, what is it the remote PIC's responsibility to determine?

options.A: That an aviation medical examiner has issued a medical certificate
options.B: That a visual observer is trained to take over the controls
options.C: That the aircraft's manufacturer has approved the flight
options.D: That the medical condition is under control and the remote PIC can safely conduct a small UA operation

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says medical conditions "such as epilepsy, may also create a risk to operations" and that "It is the remote PIC’s responsibility to determine that their medical condition is under control and they can safely conduct a small UA operation."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what ordinarily cures acute fatigue?

options.A: Treatment by a physician
options.B: Rest after exertion and 8 hours of sound sleep
options.C: A short break between flights
options.D: A caffeinated drink before the flight

questions.explanation: Acute fatigue is short term, and "Rest after exertion and 8 hours of sound sleep ordinarily cures this condition."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: If fatigue occurs during the operation of a small UA, what does the Study Guide say about training and experience?

options.A: Experienced pilots can overcome it by concentrating harder
options.B: No amount of training or experience can overcome the detrimental effects
options.C: Recurrent training removes its effects
options.D: Its effects are overcome once the pilot has flown the same aircraft many times

questions.explanation: "If fatigue occurs during the operation of a small UA, no amount of training or experience can overcome the detrimental effects."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: A tired remote pilot seems to fly each part of a task as usual, but the timing of each part is slightly off, so the whole operation is less smooth. Which effect of skill fatigue does the Study Guide describe this way?

options.A: Disruption of the perceptual field
options.B: Hyperventilation
options.C: Chronic fatigue
options.D: Timing disruption

questions.explanation: Skill fatigue has two main effects; one is "Timing disruption—appearing to perform a task as usual, but the timing of each component is slightly off."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Why does the Study Guide say a certain amount of stress is good?

options.A: It keeps a person alert and prevents complacency
options.B: It removes the need for rest before a flight
options.C: Its effects never add up over time
options.D: It makes performance rise without limit

questions.explanation: "A certain amount of stress is good since it keeps a person alert and prevents complacency." The Study Guide adds that effects of stress "are cumulative".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what is the problem with relying on the thirst mechanism to prevent dehydration?

options.A: It is triggered only by caffeine and alcohol
options.B: It starts before any fluid has been lost
options.C: It arrives too late, and a small amount of fluid in the mouth turns it off
options.D: It works only at high altitudes

questions.explanation: "The problem is that the thirst mechanism arrives too late", and "A small amount of fluid in the mouth turns this mechanism off and the replacement of needed body fluid is delayed."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Fitness to fly and the medical condition rule
questions.question: The morning after drinking, a remote pilot with a hangover feels he is functioning normally. What does the Study Guide say about this situation?

options.A: He is still under the influence of alcohol, and motor and mental response impairment is still present
options.B: Feeling normal shows that the alcohol has left his body
options.C: A hangover affects only hearing, not vision or reflexes
options.D: A hangover is a sign of dehydration only, not of alcohol

questions.explanation: "While experiencing a hangover, a pilot is still under the influence of alcohol. Although a pilot may think he or she is functioning normally, motor and mental response impairment is still present."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Fitness to fly and the medical condition rule
questions.question: Besides approved medications, which products does the Study Guide say are derived from substances often found in medications and could also have adverse side effects?

options.A: Only prescription drugs approved by the FDA
options.B: Herbal and dietary supplements, sport and energy boosters, and some other "natural" products
options.C: Bottled water and sport drink flavoring
options.D: No other products; only medications have side effects

questions.explanation: "Additionally, herbal and dietary supplements, sport and energy boosters, and some other “natural” products are derived from substances often found in medications that could also have adverse side effects."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: For severe heat stress conditions, what drinking rate does the Study Guide give?

options.A: One quart every 24 hours
options.B: One cup every two hours
options.C: Four quarts per hour
options.D: One quart per hour

questions.explanation: "Individuals should drink one quart per hour for severe heat stress conditions or one pint per hour for moderate stress conditions."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: The Study Guide's risk management principles tell pilots to accept no unnecessary risk. What reason does it give?

options.A: All risk can be removed from flying with enough planning
options.B: Unnecessary risk is acceptable only during preflight planning
options.C: Flying is not possible without risk, but unnecessary risk comes without a corresponding return
options.D: Any risk at all makes a flight unlawful under Part 107

questions.explanation: The principle reads: "Accept no unnecessary risk. Flying is not possible without risk, but unnecessary risk comes without a corresponding return."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Risk assessment, PAVE and external pressures
questions.question: Why does the Study Guide say a single pilot has a greater vulnerability than a full crew when assessing risk?

options.A: A single pilot always flies longer missions
options.B: A single pilot is not allowed to use checklists
options.C: A single pilot cannot set personal minimums
options.D: With no other crew member for consultation, the single pilot must wrestle with the intangible factors that draw one into a hazardous position

questions.explanation: "The single pilot who has no other crew member for consultation must wrestle with the intangible factors that draw one into a hazardous position. Therefore, he or she has a greater vulnerability than a full crew."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Risk assessment, PAVE and external pressures
questions.question: As used in the Study Guide's PAVE discussion, what are personal minimums?

options.A: Limits unique to that individual pilot's current level of experience and proficiency
options.B: The lowest weather values allowed by Part 107
options.C: The minimum number of crew members required for a flight
options.D: Fixed limits that are the same for every remote pilot

questions.explanation: Pilots can "set personal minimums for items in each risk category. These are limits unique to that individual pilot’s current level of experience and proficiency."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Risk assessment, PAVE and external pressures
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, why is management of external pressure the single most important key to risk management?

options.A: It is the only risk factor that Part 107 regulates
options.B: It is the one risk factor category that can cause a pilot to ignore all the other risk factors
options.C: External pressures affect crews but never a single pilot
options.D: External pressures disappear once a visual observer is added

questions.explanation: "Management of external pressure is the single most important key to risk management because it is the one risk factor category that can cause a pilot to ignore all the other risk factors."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Decision-making models and crew resource management
questions.question: A remote pilot who flies alone asks what Single-Pilot Resource Management (SRM) is meant to teach. According to the Study Guide, SRM is all about helping pilots learn how to do what?

options.A: Repair the small UA in the field without a technician
options.B: Memorize the radio frequencies of every nearby airport
options.C: Gather information, analyze it, and make decisions
options.D: Replace the visual observer with automation

questions.explanation: "SRM is all about helping pilots learn how to gather information, analyze it, and make decisions."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Decision-making models and crew resource management
questions.question: Pressed for time in an emergency, an experienced pilot takes the first workable option that comes to mind instead of comparing the pros and cons of each approach. What does the Study Guide call this type of decision-making?

options.A: Naturalistic or automatic decision-making
options.B: The DECIDE model
options.C: The 5P model
options.D: Analytical decision-making

questions.explanation: "Experts take the first workable option they can find." The terms "naturalistic" and "automatic decision-making" describe this type, which is "most often used in times of emergencies".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Decision-making models and crew resource management
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how does Single-Pilot Resource Management (SRM) training help a pilot maintain situational awareness?

options.A: By having the visual observer take over all navigation tasks
options.B: By replacing preflight planning with checks made during the flight
options.C: By limiting each flight to a single task
options.D: By managing the automation and associated aircraft control and navigation tasks

questions.explanation: "SRM training helps the pilot maintain situational awareness by managing the automation and associated aircraft control and navigation tasks. This enables the pilot to accurately assess and manage risk and make accurate and timely decisions."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Using the scanning technique in the Study Guide, where should a pilot begin scanning, and which way should the scan move?

options.A: At the position of the aircraft, moving outward to the greatest distance
options.B: At the greatest distance an object can be perceived (top), moving inward toward the position of the aircraft (bottom)
options.C: Straight overhead, moving down to the horizon on one side only
options.D: Wherever the last aircraft was seen, without moving the eyes

questions.explanation: Pilots "must look from right to left or left to right" and "should begin scanning at the greatest distance an object can be perceived (top) and move inward toward the position of the aircraft (bottom)."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what is the first effect of high workload?

options.A: The pilot's situational awareness improves
options.B: The pilot can give full attention to several tasks at one time
options.C: The pilot may be working harder but accomplishing less
options.D: The pilot receives more input from various sources

questions.explanation: "The first effect of high workload is that the pilot may be working harder but accomplishing less."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)
